I'm making the scrape.yaml port match http-metrics and keeping the deploy rather than reverting it. I'm also considering a test that reads both yaml files to check they agree, and since PyYAML may not be available, I'm leaning toward simple text parsing.

I'm going to make the test read the port from the values file and check it against scrape.yaml using plain text matching, so there's no PyYAML dependency.

The ServiceMonitor in deploy/scrape.yaml still targets the old port name `metrics`, which the deploy renamed to `http-metrics`. I'm pointing the scrape at the new name and adding a test that checks the two files agree.

input.explanation:
The fault: `deploy/scrape.yaml` says it picks the endpoint to scrape by the port's name (`endpoints: - port: metrics`). Its own comment says that name has to match `metrics.portName` in `deploy/values-production.yaml`, and that nothing checks the two agree. A name that matches no port leaves Prometheus with no targets, and nothing reports an error. Deploy 9f4ad14 renamed the port to `http-metrics` in values-production.yaml but did not change scrape.yaml, so the selector matched nothing. That is why the metrics stopped while the service kept serving.

The fix: change the ServiceMonitor endpoint to `port: http-metrics`, so it matches the name the deploy now gives the port. The deploy stays in place, nothing is reverted.

The test: I added `tests/io_shop/test_scrape_config.py` to cover the missing check. It reads `metrics.portName` from values-production.yaml and every `port:` entry under the ServiceMonitor's `endpoints` in scrape.yaml, using plain line parsing so it needs no YAML library. It asserts that every scraped port name equals the configured portName. Against the current files it should fail ('metrics' vs 'http-metrics'). With this change it should pass, and it will catch the next rename that updates only one of the two files.

# How the platform's Prometheus collects the shop's metrics.
#
# The ServiceMonitor the platform applies with the shop's chart, kept in the
# repository beside how the shop is deployed, so that how it is collected
# changes in the same pull request as what it is collected from.
#
# It selects the shop's Service by label, then the endpoint to scrape on that
# Service by the port's *name* - never its number - so a port can move without
# anything here being touched.
#
# The name here has to be the one `metrics.portName` in values-production.yaml
# gives the port. Nothing checks that the two agree: a name that matches no port
# is not an error to the operator, it is a target list with nothing in it.
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
  name: io-shop
  labels:
    release: prometheus
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: io-shop
  endpoints:
    - port: http-metrics
      path: /metrics
      interval: 15s

input.summary: Point the ServiceMonitor at the renamed metrics port (http-metrics) and test that scrape.yaml and values-production.yaml agree
